pkg.desc: The built-in PKG Manager is a separate daemon with its own UI (port 8844) that installs PKGs from USB / disc / SMB shares. The "PKG Install" sidebar item starts it automatically and takes you straight to its UI.
pkg.frame_first_run: First start may take a few seconds
pkg.frame_fail_hint: Make sure elfldr is running on port 9021; you can also check the PKG Manager card on the Settings page.
pkg.launch_ok: Launch command sent, first start takes a few seconds
pkg.stop_hint: Stop the PKG Manager daemon (you can start it again anytime)
pkg.upload_ok: Uploaded v{{ver}}, takes effect after restarting PKG Manager
pkg.upload_hint: Updates are manual: open this page from a desktop browser and select a newer pkg-manager ELF. Uploads are validated (ELF header + version signature) and committed atomically; the embedded baseline is an offline fallback and never overwrites an uploaded file.
entries.desc: Quick-access list for common plugins and LAN services (e.g. http://192.168.1.100:8844). Entries are stored on the console, so phone / desktop / PS5 all see the same list; a green dot means the address is currently reachable.
entries.name: Name
entries.url_hint: Scheme may be omitted (defaults to http://); write https:// explicitly when needed.
entries.empty: No entries yet. Click "Add Entry" to get started.
app.dashboard.subtitle: Pick a payload below to launch it on your PS5.
settings.theme_desc: Choose dark or light interface; "Auto" follows your system preference.
settings.donate_desc: This is a fork maintained by naye, based on the original Payload Manager by itsPLK (v0.5.1.61). If you like it, you can buy the original author a coffee.
donate.description: If you like this project, you can support the original author. Thank you very much!
donate.fork_desc: This is a fork of Payload Manager maintained by {{maintainer}}.
donate.fork_donate_note: Donations through the button above go to the original author (itsPLK), not this fork.
donate.ref_desc: Changes in this fork were informed by the open-source projects below, each attributed to its author with the exact source location.
donate.sdk_hwinfo: Official SDK sample showing that host model and serial number are just two plain libkernel calls (sceKernelGetHwModelName / sceKernelGetHwSerialNumber) — no privilege escalation, no inst0.dat. This fork's hardware info sources were reworked accordingly.
donate.sdk_priv: Official privilege pattern (temporarily set authid/caps, always restore) plus read-only kernel constants such as TARGETID / SECURITY_FLAGS / UTOKEN_FLAGS; it also explains the root cause of our .53 crash.
donate.sdk_stubs: SDK stub library, used to verify which hardware APIs are genuine libkernel exports (they live in libkernel_sys.c, not libkernel.c).
donate.uploadsuite: On-device proof that the two APIs above return a real CFI-xxxx model string; also warns that sceKernelIccGet* crash and that Sony sensor APIs are not reentrant (serialize and throttle them).
donate.hwinfo: Field layout of the struct returned by sceKernelGetProsperoSystemSwVersion (version[0x1c] + raw), used for firmware version string parsing.
donate.ps5debugng: Its PROTOCOL.md and FW_VERSION implementation gave an independent cross-check of our BCD firmware decoding, and its vendored SDK stubs were used to verify the symbol table.

settings.read_hw_desc: Read and show PS5 hardware info (temperature, fan, memory, VRAM, storage) on the dashboard. When off, those cards show a dash.
